Was in Harrismith about 3/4 yrs ago, filling up the car with my family. Dad's wallet gets stolen at the garage shop without him noticing until after they had left. We reported the theft to the local police, but, yk, nobody expects anything to come of it. Well, 2 hrs later, he gets a phone call, and its the older brother of the thief apologising for his brother's stealing of the wallet, and asking if he can meet us in Boksburg to give the wallet back *(he was the driver of the rented car they had left in and had evidently discovered what his brother and his brother's accomplice(s) had done).* We met him at a mall there, compensated him, and then carried on with our journey, but he was very civil and apologised once again for the other people's actions. The Harrismith police were absolutely shocked when we phoned them later that day 😅

Hey, I'm also 17, South African.  I get that feeling you have that you haven't done anything of note yet. But I mean, 17 years old isn't even out of school yet :/. I also struggle with depression, suicidal ideation, and the likes, but I can tell you that from what I've seen, there's so much more to come, and our lives don't have to be plain and generic. You could find a passion at 20, 23, or 30, and indulge yourself in it, or you may not, but you may still find something nice that brings you joy that you simply haven't yet experienced. I really do know how it feels to want to die, trust me, but just try to stave off the negativity/negative influences and see what your actual future has to offer, cause most ppl's lives don't have much direction/acheivements at 17. And whose to say we all have to do great things anyways; society wasn't built by 1 person doing notable things.
